chunks: A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Khalid, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Abi Nasr, from Safwan ibn Mihran, from Aamir ibn al-Simt, from Habib ibn Abi Thabit, from Ali ibn al-Husayn (peace be upon him) who said:

Prejudice (bias) would not admit anyone to Paradise except the prejudice of Hamza ibn Abd al-Muttalib, and that is when he embraced Islam out of anger for the Prophet (peace be upon him and his family) regarding the story of the camel's stomach contents which were thrown upon the Prophet (peace be upon him and his family).

key_terms.السَّلَى: The stomach contents of a camel
key_terms.حَمْزَةُ بْنُ عَبْدِ الْمُطَّلِبِ: Hamza ibn Abd al-Muttalib, the uncle of the Prophet
key_terms.لِلنَّبِيِّ: For the Prophet (indicating zeal for his honor)

ai.seo_question: What is the exception to prejudice (hamiyyah) being excluded from Paradise in Shia hadith?
ai.summary: In this hadith from al-Kafi, Imam Ali ibn al-Husayn (Zayn al-Abidin) clarifies that the general prohibition of 'al-hamiyyah' (tribal zeal or bias) applies to all except Hamza ibn Abd al-Muttalib, whose prejudice was righteous and specific to defending the Prophet's honor. This exception occurred during the 'Hadith al-Sala' incident, where the Quraysh threw the stomach contents of a slaughtered camel on the Prophet, prompting Hamza's angry conversion to Islam. This distinction highlights how context and intent transform a potentially negative trait into a virtue in Shia scholarship.

en.hubeali:
A number of our companions, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad Bin Khalid, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad Bin Abu Nasr, from Safwan Bin Mihran, from Aamir Bin Al Simt, from habeeb Bin Abu Sabit, 
(It has been narrated) from Ali<sup>asws</sup> Bin Al-Husayn<sup>asws</sup> having said:

‘A prejudice would not be entering the Paradise except that of Hamza<sup>as</sup> Bin Abdul Muttalib<sup>as</sup>, and that is when he<sup>as</sup> was among Muslims, he<sup>as</sup> got angry when an amusing discussion (which took place) against the Prophet<sup>saww</sup> – (which was) regarding the camel’s stomach contents which were thrown upon the Prophet<sup>saww</sup>’.
en.sarwar: 5. A number of our people have narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Khalid from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn abu Nasr from Safwan ibn Mehran from ‘Amir ibn al-Simt from Habib ibn abu Thabit from Ali ibn al-Husayn (a.s.) who has said the following: “

Tribal and racist feelings will not enter paradise except that of Hamza ibn ‘Abd al-Muttalib. When he accepted Islam he expressed such angered feelings over the story of the contents of a camel’s stomach poured over the Holy Prophet.”
